drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What is the main problem: testicular pain or swelling, a lump, penile sores or discharge, erection problems, or a bulge in the groin?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main male genital complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: When did this start, and is it getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Sudden testicular pain is treated as torsion until proven otherwise.

questions.text: Is there pain in a testicle, and did it start suddenly?
questions.rationale: Acute unilateral testicular pain is a surgical emergency until torsion is excluded.

questions.text: Is one testicle swollen, high-riding, or different in size or firmness?
questions.rationale: Swelling and lie of the testis help separate torsion, epididymitis, and tumor.

questions.text: Have you felt a lump on a testicle, and is it painless and growing?
questions.rationale: A painless testicular mass is cancer until proven otherwise.

questions.text: With the testicular pain, have you had nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain?
questions.rationale: Nausea with acute testicular pain supports torsion.

questions.text: Any burning with urine, discharge from the penis, or sores?
questions.rationale: Discharge and dysuria suggest urethritis or STI rather than torsion.

questions.text: Have you had any new sexual partners or unprotected sex recently?
questions.rationale: Sexual history frames STI and epididymo-orchitis risk.

questions.text: Have you had fever or chills with the genital symptoms?
questions.rationale: Fever suggests epididymo-orchitis, abscess, or Fournier gangrene.

questions.text: Is the scrotal skin red, very tender, spreading, or dark, especially if you have diabetes?
questions.rationale: Rapidly progressive scrotal infection can be necrotizing and is an emergency.

questions.text: Do you have a bulge in the groin that comes and goes, and is it stuck, painful, or red?
questions.rationale: An incarcerated or strangulated hernia needs urgent surgical care.

questions.text: Did you injure the testicles, penis, or groin?
questions.rationale: Trauma can cause rupture, hematoma, or urethral injury.

questions.text: Are you having trouble getting or keeping an erection, and is that new?
questions.rationale: Erectile dysfunction may be vascular, neurologic, hormonal, or medication-related.

questions.text: Have you had an erection lasting more than four hours, or one that is painful?
questions.rationale: Priapism is a time-sensitive emergency.

questions.text: Is there curvature, pain with erection, or a lump along the shaft?
questions.rationale: These features suggest Peyronie's disease or other penile pathology.

questions.text: If uncircumcised, can you retract the foreskin, or is the head of the penis trapped?
questions.rationale: Paraphimosis is an emergency; phimosis can cause infection and retention.

questions.text: Any trouble starting urine, weak stream, or waking at night to pee?
questions.rationale: Voiding symptoms may belong with the urinary bank but often accompany genital complaints.

questions.text: Any back pain, weight loss, or swollen legs with a testicular or prostate concern?
questions.rationale: These can indicate advanced testicular or prostate cancer.

questions.text: Have you had mumps, or a recent viral illness with testicular pain?
questions.rationale: Viral orchitis is a classic cause of testicular pain after puberty.

questions.text: Do you take blood pressure medicines, antidepressants, testosterone, or injections for erections?
questions.rationale: Many drugs affect erections, libido, and priapism risk.

questions.text: Do you have diabetes, heart disease, or smoking history?
questions.rationale: Vascular disease is a leading cause of erectile dysfunction.

questions.text: Did you have an undescended testicle, or surgery on a testicle as a child?
questions.rationale: Cryptorchidism raises testicular cancer risk.

questions.text: How is this affecting pain, sex, work, or walking?
questions.rationale: Functional impact and unrelenting pain guide urgency.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Sudden severe testicular pain
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe sudden severe pain in a testicle, especially with swelling or nausea?

red_flags.label: Painless testicular lump
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a painless or growing lump on a testicle?

red_flags.label: Spreading red or dark scrotal skin with illness
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report rapidly spreading redness, darkness, or severe pain of the scrotal skin, especially with diabetes or fever?

red_flags.label: Stuck painful groin bulge
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe a groin bulge that will not go back in and is painful or red?

red_flags.label: Erection lasting more than four hours
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a prolonged or painful erection lasting hours?

red_flags.label: Foreskin trapped behind the head of the penis
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report the foreskin stuck behind the head of the penis with swelling?
